newsitem.title: USA: Delmarva Power holders approve merger.
newsitem.headline: Delmarva Power holders approve merger.

text.p: The merger of Delmarva Power & Light Co and Atlantic Energy Co was approved by Delmarva shareholders at a special meeting Thursday.
Delmarva Chief Executive Howard Cosgrove told Reuters that preliminary results indicated Atlantic shareholders would also approve the merger at a meeting today.

"Shareholders have approved the merger. That is the first step," Cosgrove said in an interview following the Delmarva meeting. "The next step is approval by the Federal Regulatory Energy Commission (and state regulatory agencies)."
"Some filings have already been made. Others will be made in mid-February. We expect approval at the earliest by the end of 1997 or, more realistically, in the first quarter of 1998," he said.
"It's important that we move forward with a combined business strategy," Cosgrove said.
Cosgrove said that when the merger is completed, about 10 percent of the combined workforce, or 400 people, would lose their jobs.
Under the merger, shareholders of Delmarva will receive one share of stock in the new company, to be named Conectiv Inc, for each share of Delmarva they now hold.
Atlantic shareholders will receive 3/4 share of Conectiv plus 1/8 share of Class A stock for each share of Atlantic they hold.
Delmarva Chief Financial Officer Barbara Graham said shareholders of both companies will continue to receive the same dividend of $1.54 a share annually after the merger.
The dividend for Atlantic shareholders will be a pro-rated percentage of the dividends for the new Class A and common stock.
Graham said Morgan Stanley had estimated the Conectiv stock would begin trading at about $20, and that the Class A stock would pay a dividend of $3.20 a year for three years.
"The combined company is in a stronger position to support the dividend going forward," Graham told Reuters.
